slides.title: Statement and Proof of Jensen's Inequality
bullets: Let F be convex on convex set X
X is a random vector with finite expectation in X
slides.speakerNotes: Present the formal statement of Jensen's Inequality and highlight the convexity and expectation conditions.
slides.latex:
\begin{theorem}[Jensen's Inequality]
Let \( F: \mathcal{X} \to \mathbb{R} \) be a convex function defined on a convex set \( \mathcal{X} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n \), and let \( \mathbf{X} \) be a random vector taking values in \( \mathcal{X} \) with finite expectation \( \mathbb{E}[\mathbf{X}] \in \mathcal{X} \). Then
\[
F\big(\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{X}]\big) \leq \mathbb{E}[F(\mathbf{X})].
\]
\end{theorem}

slides.title: Proof Sketch of Jensen's Inequality

slides.speakerNotes: Explain the key steps of the proof using subgradients and linearity of expectation to derive the inequality.
